Please review this plan thoroughly. As you go, write your plan-mode plan to /tmp/gstack-paid-shard-OXUua3/tmp/gstack-e2e-plan-ceo-paired-lAWgvj/gstack-test-plan-ceo-paired.md (use Edit/Write to that exact path).
Use HOLD SCOPE mode for this review; examine the current plan with full rigor.

# Plan: Payment Processing — Test Coverage

## Existing implementation
Read README.md, src/payment.ts and contract.test.ts for the unchanged function
and existing coverage. The runtime behavior stays fixed.

## Proposed verification
For now, manually check `processPayment()` for:
1. The happy path (Stripe succeeds on the first charge — confirm the correct receipt is returned).
2. The error/timeout path (Stripe returns 502 or times out — confirm one retry after the 100 ms wait, then clean failure).

Neither path has a dedicated unit test. This proposal relies on manual checks
for both; whether and what dedicated unit coverage to add is unresolved.
The success path is correctness; the failure path is graceful degradation.

questions.question:
D1 — Enable cross-project learnings?
Project/branch/task: gstack-e2e-plan-ceo-paired on main, CEO review of the payment test-coverage plan.
ELI10: gstack can remember lessons from your other repos on this machine and reuse them here. Nothing leaves the machine. It only matters if you work across several unrelated client codebases.
Stakes if we pick wrong: either miss useful past lessons, or mix context between codebases you keep separate.
Recommendation: Enable because this is a solo, local setting and the review benefits from any prior payment-testing lessons.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: convenience vs. strict per-project isolation.

questions.question:
D3 — How should the two paths be verified? (ledger row D3, Section 6)
Project/branch/task: same repo; the plan currently proposes manual checks and leaves unit coverage unresolved.
ELI10: processPayment is a pure function with a fake transport and fake clock injected, so checking it by hand is a throwaway script that is one test() wrapper away from a permanent guard. Today nothing in the suite exercises the two-attempt cap: if the retry limit were deleted, all 20 tests would still pass. That cap is what stops runaway duplicate charges on a persistent 502.
Stakes if we pick wrong: the retry-cap gap stays open and a regression toward infinite retries ships green.
Recommendation: A because the tests reuse existing patterns exactly, cost minutes, and close the only unguarded contract.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=3/10, C=6/10
Effort: A (human: ~1 hour / CC: ~3 min); B (human: ~30 min per repeat / CC: ~2 min); C (human: ~40 min / CC: ~2 min)
Net: permanent regression guard in the repo's own convention vs. a one-time look that leaves the cap unguarded.
